sources.title: Introducing GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Original December 11, 2025 announcement makes the models available that day and explicitly maps GPT-5.2 Instant to gpt-5.2-chat-latest, separately from Thinking and Pro. The Instant API release is explicit; the xhigh reasoning controls described there apply to Thinking and Pro.

sources.title: GPT-5.2 Chat API documentation
sources.evidence: Exact alias documentation lists text/image input, text output, 128,000 context, 16,384 maximum output, Chat Completions/Responses and function calling. It also lists a contradictory 272,000 maximum input. It marks the model shut down and lists only the undated alias; no reasoning or prompt-caching feature flag is present.

sources.title: Update to GPT-5 System Card: GPT-5.2
sources.evidence: Downloaded the original December 11, 2025 card, searched its full text and inspected training and exact Instant comparison columns. Separates Instant and Thinking; reports Instant safety, vision and health results but no total/active count or detailed architecture. Generic reasoning-training prose is not treated as proof about Instant.

sources.title: GPT-5.5 Instant System Card
sources.evidence: Downloaded and searched the May 4, 2026 card and inspected its exact GPT-5.2 Instant safety, vision and health comparison columns. These disclose benchmark results, not parameter counts or network structure; the card warns that previous-model results can reflect later versions. GPT-5.5-specific reasoning details are not transferred.

sources.title: Investigating the consequences of accidentally grading CoT during RL
sources.evidence: May 7, 2026 training research explicitly identifies GPT-5.2 Instant among released models whose chain of thought was inadvertently graded during reinforcement learning. It qualifies GPT-5 Instant models as having at most limited CoT. This provides exact-variant reasoning evidence, but no parameter count or detailed architecture.

sources.title: Prompt caching
sources.evidence: Current guide explains caching and lists gpt-5.2 among models supporting extended retention, but does not name gpt-5.2-chat-latest in that list. Support for the distinct Thinking alias is not transferred to this Chat alias as structural evidence.

sources.title: Prompt Caching 201
sources.evidence: Archived guide explicitly covers models before GPT-5.6 and explains caching through Transformer attention key/value tensors. Its model table names gpt-5.2, not the Chat alias. Together with cached-input pricing alone, it does not establish exact Instant structure under this audit evidence standard.

sources.title: File inputs
sources.evidence: Directly read guide: Responses handles PDFs by extracting text and page images for vision-capable models; Chat Completions also accepts PDF file content. Applied to this exact model’s documented vision and endpoint support, this establishes PDF as an API input format, not a separate native sensory modality.

sources.title: API deprecations
sources.evidence: May 8, 2026 notice names gpt-5.2-chat-latest and gives August 10, 2026 as its shutdown date. The exact current model page independently marks it shut down. Documentation was checked; no authenticated endpoint operation was tested.

sources.title: API changelog
sources.evidence: February 10, 2026 entry explicitly updates gpt-5.2-chat-latest to the latest model used in ChatGPT. Confirms a mutable alias rather than an immutable December checkpoint; no dated OpenAI snapshot is supplied by the current exact model page.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: Current agreement grants limited hosted-service use and reserves service intellectual property in section 9.1. Supports a descriptive proprietary classification, not a downloadable-weight license or an assertion that current contract wording applied on launch day.

sources.title: All OpenAI API models
sources.evidence: Current model catalog lists GPT-5.2 Chat as shut down and separately identifies its Apache-2.0 open-weight gpt-oss releases. GPT-5.2 Chat is documented as a hosted model, with no released weight distribution in the reviewed publisher materials.

sources.title: Azure models sold directly by Azure
sources.evidence: Exact gpt-5.2-chat rows for 2025-12-11 and 2026-02-10 independently specify a 128,000 context, 111,616 input and 16,384 output, plus tool/function calling. These corroborate historical context, but Azure-specific version labels and retirement dates are not assigned to OpenAI’s endpoint.

name.note: Official API model name; the original launch binds this alias to GPT-5.2 Instant.

developer.note: First-party release and system card identify the developer.

family.note: GPT-5.2 release family within the wider GPT-5 series; this is the Instant/Chat variant, not Thinking or the ChatGPT router.

release_date.note: Original dated announcement explicitly makes GPT-5.2 Instant available that day as this API alias; later alias updates do not replace the initial release date.

open_weights.note: Publisher documents hosted ChatGPT/API distribution under retained service rights and separately identifies its downloadable open-weight releases.

license.note: Descriptive hosted-model classification, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total model parameter count in the reviewed original card, exact later Instant comparisons or first-party training research. Benchmark values and sibling model specifications are not counts for this variant.

active_parameters_b.note: No active-parameter count or expert layout is disclosed for exact GPT-5.2 Instant in the reviewed sources; neither a dense assumption nor another model’s count is substituted.

architecture.note: Targeted first-party training and interpretability searches did not yield an exact structural disclosure. Exact Chat docs show cached-input pricing but no caching feature binding; the pre-5.6 KV-cache mechanism alone is insufficient to assign Transformer to this variant. No dense/MoE inference.

context_window.note: The exact OpenAI HTML and Markdown model pages specify 128,000 context; Azure exact-version rows corroborate it. OpenAI Markdown also says 272,000 maximum input, an unresolved contradiction; this is not used to inflate the explicitly named context. Output limit is 16,384.

modalities.note: Native model modalities are text/image input and text output. PDF is included as the API file format processed into text and page images, justified by exact vision and Responses/Chat Completions support; no native audio/video claim.

reasoning.note: Launch binds this alias to GPT-5.2 Instant; later OpenAI RL research explicitly reports CoT grading for that exact variant and qualifies Instant CoT as limited. This supports reasoning capability, not user-configurable effort levels, adaptive reasoning, or routing to the separate Thinking model.

tool_call.note: Exact model documentation explicitly supports function calling; Azure’s exact variant rows independently corroborate it. This describes last-documented capability, not current endpoint availability.

description.value: GPT-5.2 Instant chat model with text and image input, text output and function calling in the API.
description.note: Plain factual variant and capability description, without generic workflow claims or specifications transferred from Thinking.

patch.notes: The original 2025-12-11 launch maps gpt-5.2-chat-latest to GPT-5.2 Instant, separately from Thinking and Pro. This was a mutable alias, explicitly updated on 2026-02-10; the current OpenAI model page lists no dated immutable snapshot. Exact OpenAI documentation specifies 128,000 context and 16,384 maximum output, but its Markdown also gives an inconsistent 272,000 maximum input; Azure exact-version rows corroborate 128,000 context. OpenAI training research explicitly establishes limited CoT for GPT-5.2 Instant; reasoning=true does not imply documented effort controls, adaptive reasoning or the ChatGPT router. PDF denotes API conversion to extracted text and page images. Total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed in the reviewed original card, later exact Instant comparisons and training research; architecture remains unverified. OpenAI’s deprecation notice gives 2026-08-10 as this alias’s shutdown date, consistent with its current model page. Specifications are historical documentation, not a successful endpoint test.

summary: Confirmed original December 11, 2025 Instant API release, 128K context, vision and function calling; corrected family, proprietary classification, PDF API format and description. Exact later training research supports limited-CoT reasoning without borrowing Thinking features. Recorded mutable-alias update, 272K input/context documentation conflict and August 10, 2026 shutdown. Total/active parameter counts remain undisclosed and architecture unverified.
